As of 156 PM EST Tuesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Surface high pressure will continue to build 
into the region this afternoon, with sharply colder temperatures
this afternoon in comparison to the last several days. The 
center of the surface high will shift directly overhead tonight,
with ideal radiational cooling conditions expected. The clear 
skies and calm winds will allow low temperatures Wednesday 
morning to drop into the teens for most areas, except locally in
the 20s along and in the immediate vicinity of Lake Champlain. 
Highs Wednesday will be a few degrees warmer than Tuesday, but 
still mainly in the 30s to low 40s. Dry conditions are expected 
to continue into the first half of Thursday, with no impactful 
weather currently expected Tuesday or Wednesday for any holiday 
travel plans.

KEY MESSAGE 2: A low pressure system is expected to track 
northward along the East Coast and into our region the night of 
Thanksgiving into Friday. Most guidance continues to support 
widespread rainfall with this event, with some freezing rain or 
wintry mix possible at the start, especially across higher 
elevations and colder hollows. With such a dry airmass in place 
ahead of the system, it may take some time for precipitation to 
reach the ground with the potential for some significant wet-
bulb cooling, which may allow for a little more wintry mix at 
the onset of precipitation. Model guidance and sounding support 
freezing rain as the most likely wintry precipitation type, but 
a period of sleet or just a true mix cannot be ruled out. No 
significant impacts from wintry precipitation are anticipated at
this time, with a light glaze of ice to a few hundredths in 
areas that see a period of freezing rain, although some holiday 
travel impacts may be possible late Thursday. As previously 
mentioned, rain is expected to be the dominant precipitation 
type with this event. Current forecast rainfall amounts are 
generally between 0.5 to 1.0 inches of rain, with higher amounts
expected further south towards Southern New England. Given the 
prolonged period of dryness across the region, this rainfall 
will be largely beneficial. 

In addition to the precipitation, strong south to southeast 
winds will be possible, especially across the higher terrain. 
The low level jet enters the region Thursday night and looks to 
drop down to around 5,000 ft in the in the northern Greens but 
down to around 3,000-4000 ft in the southern Greens. Summit 
winds will be very strong, and gusty downslope winds will be 
possible along the western slopes of the southern Greens, 
especially if precipitation winds down and we get into a dry 
slot.

KEY MESSAGE 3: 

Early in the weekend (Friday night into Saturday morning) the 
departure of deep low pressure will support the greatest chances
of snow as precipitation type during the period, but even this 
will be minimal. While details are difficult to provide in this 
time range, temperatures and moisture will be very marginal for 
snow. The best ingredients for a lowering of snow levels will 
also be contingent on the track of the trailing upper level low.
Generally spread in snow level guidance is moderately high, 
with the 10th and 90th percentiles of about 1200 feet to 3600 
feet, suggesting that some high terrain snow showers are likely,
while there is a low chance of any precipitation being snow in 
the valleys even as temperatures get a little cooler during this
period. Upslope does not look favorable at this time with 
thermal profiles warming aloft on Saturday as upper level 
ridging quickly moves in. 

Thereafter, there will probably be a period of at least 
scattered rain showers ahead of a clipper system. However, there
is large spread in timing/duration of any rain, associated with
the possible development of a Colorado low which could instead 
be the primary low pressure system. The PoPs reflect this 
scenario, with somewhat higher chances of precipitation on 
Monday as opposed to Sunday. Regardless, milder south winds can 
be expected with low pressure tracking to our north. With its 
passage, Tuesday will trend cooler but at this time the pattern 
greatly favors continued above normal temperatures for the end 
of November.
